A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-encoder study. All 17 pages of each version, including supplementary Sections A–F, tables, equations, and figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original metadata-prediction experiments, semantic classification and retrieval results, and supplementary augmentation and masking analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised acquisition-prediction and masking results in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The frozen-encoder probes, kNN classification and retrieval procedures, and augmentation-training approach are retained. The masking revisions concern experimental controls rather than a new proposed model, objective, or algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet, iNaturalist 2018, FlickrExif, PairCams, supplementary ImageNet-ES evaluation, and YFCC15M augmentation training. Processing/acquisition prediction and semantic classification/retrieval coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces DINO RN50 with MoCov3 ViT-B in the neighborhood comparison. Although both methods already appear in the overall encoder inventory, their participation in this particular comparison changes; the overall 47-encoder inventory remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 and new footnote 6 revise a central acquisition-evaluation control: masked experiments now use equal resize and center-crop sizes and apply masking after cropping. The main masking ratio changes from 90% to 95%, described as equivalent under the earlier implementation. This materially changes the cross-encoder evaluation conditions. Table 2 also switches the supervised ConvNeXt configuration from L to B.

E4.justification: Existing analyses are revised: Figure 5 reassesses semantic suppression by masking, Figure B updates the acquisition-related augmentation ablation, and Figure F updates the 75% masking analysis. These revisit established questions without adding a new family of ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ten-seed averaging descriptions in Sections 3.1 and 4.1. No changed run-count disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 6 substantially revises acquisition-prediction results: self-supervised encoders become much closer to CVLs and lead on some attributes. Figures 5, B, and F also change under revised masking conditions, so these are replacement results rather than fixed-setting performance gains. Unmasked results change too, including Figures D/E and Table 2: SigLIP ViT-B/16 at k=10 changes from 58.6% to 59.0%, and CLIP ViT-L/14@336 from 70.1% to 70.0%.

T1.justification: The processing/acquisition-label definitions, sampling constructions, and sharpening formula in Appendix B are unchanged. Neither version introduces new theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims that visual encoders preserve metadata traces, these traces affect semantic tasks, and CVLs are especially sensitive, potentially because of weaker training augmentations.

C2.justification: Figure 5's caption changes from avoiding semantic leakage to reducing it, and Section 3.2 removes the assertion that all encoders become nearly random at 90% masking. Appendix A narrows the SigLIP counterexample to attributes such as JPEG. The broader mechanism discussion and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New footnote 6 explicitly documents the revised resize/crop relationship, masking order, and relationship between the old and new masking ratios. Training hyperparameters, encoder inventory, dataset-construction details, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against robustness, attribute-detection, and visual-bias research are unchanged. Reference-page backreferences change because text reflows, without adding or removing cited research.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to Section 3.2, the masking clarification, and Appendix A's SigLIP qualification. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5 changes its legend/reference-line display and masking example; Figures 6 and B revise axes or captions, and Figure 7 has different t-SNE point layouts. Text and figures reflow locally, while the overall figure/table inventory and presentation structure remain intact.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, v2 explicitly harmonizes masked preprocessing, updates the corresponding main and supplementary evidence, and qualifies interpretations about semantic leakage and SigLIP. This improves reproducibility and interpretation. The benefit is limited because Figure 5 still shows appreciable semantic accuracy for some encoders at 95% masking, so complete isolation of acquisition traces remains unsupported.
